title: Ackless stream adapter with concurrency limiter and improved telemetry for Python SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: developers building streaming chat integrations keep getting complexity from explicit ack/nack flows, duplicated fragments, and poorly observable retry behavior. We need a compact, "ackless" adapter for the Python SDK that preserves resumability, supports idempotent emission of fragments, cooperates with backpressure, and exposes telemetry so platform and customers can reason about latency, retries, and staleness.

Goal: deliver a lightweight streaming adapter (async iterator + callback-compatible) that: 1) eliminates obligatory ack/nack plumbing for most users, 2) provides an opt-in checkpointing persistence contract for resumability, 3) includes a concurrency limiter to bound in-flight consumer tasks, and 4) emits fine-grained telemetry (watermarks, emitted-fragment-latency, retry-counters) useful for Console SLO dashboards.

Scope: implement Python SDK primitives, adapter tests, an examples notebook, lightweight migration shim for callback users, a design doc, and a GitHub PR implementing the adapter plus CI. Do not change the public sync SDK surface for non-streaming calls.

Out of scope: server-side protocol changes, non-python SDKs (TS/Go).

acceptance_criteria: Adapter exposes an async iterator that yields ChatEvent objects and requires no explicit ack/nack from the consumer
Adapter supports an optional CheckpointPersistence interface: file, redis, or user-provided callable for storing resume tokens
Concurrency limiter configurable per-call and enforced end-to-end (adapter + consumer tasks)
Telemetry emitted via SDK hooks for watermarks, emitted-fragment-latency, retry-attempts, and last-resume-token-age
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering duplicate fragment deduplication, transient network retry, and resume after disconnect
Examples: notebook and snippet demonstrating callback->iterator migration and resumable consumer
implementation_notes: Core primitives: AcklessEmitter (async iterator), IdempotentFragmentStore (in-memory dedupe by idempotency-key), ConcurrencyLimiter (async context manager)
Use asyncio.Queue with bounded size to implement backpressure; on put() when full, await until space or raise BackpressureError if configured strict
Retry behavior: surface two retry layers: network-level (exponential backoff) and logical fragment reassembly (idempotency + sequence watermark). Retries should be observable via telemetry counters

CheckpointPersistence contract: async save(token:string) and load()->string | None. Provide two concrete implementations: FileCheckpoint and RedisCheckpoint. Keep interface minimal to avoid nested config objects
Compatibility: maintain existing StreamEvent shape; adapter should be a drop-in for code that currently consumes events but will pass through ackless semantics
Edge cases: out-of-order fragments must be buffered up to a configurable window (default 5s / 100 fragments) then emitted in-order or compacted depending on config
test_plan: Unit tests for deduplication logic and concurrency limiter under synthetic high-throughput conditions
Integration test with local runti me simulating intermittent network interruptions and verifying resume via FileCheckpoint
E2E example that runs against the staging runtime and asserts no duplicate user-visible content for repeated reconnects
Load test (small scale) to measure CPU/latency delta vs existing ack/nack-based adapter and ensure no regression > 10% tail latency
Fuzz test to verify adapter resilience to malformed fragments and unexpected event types
rollout_plan: 01 - Merge behind feature flag 'ackless_stream_adapter' in sdk-py main
02 - Canary: enable for 5 internal services and monitor Console metrics (watermark latency, retry counters) for 48h
03 - Gradual ramp to 50% of streaming traffic if no regressions; collect developer feedback on ergonomics
04 - Document migration recipe in release notes and provide code snippets for callback and iterator styles
05 - Deprecation plan only if we later decide to remove ack-nack paths (future)
risks: Potential for silent data loss if customers misconfigure CheckpointPersistence and rely on transient in-memory tokens
Backpressure policy inversion: if consumers are slow, bounded queue may drop fragments unless policies are explicitly configured
Observability gaps: if telemetry hooks are not wired by integrators, diagnosing resume failures will be harder
Performance regression for very large fragment bursts if ordering window is too large; must tune defaults conservatively
